Modeling ethnic differences via drug-predicted clearance from chemical structures.

The authors developed a machine-learning approach that predicts drug clearance from chemical structures and uses it to assess the risk of ethnic differences in pharmacokinetics at early drug-discovery stages. This complements mechanistic methods like PBPK modeling by enabling screening with limited experimental data.

Toll-Like Receptors in Mycoplasma Infections: Immunopathogenesis, Cheminformatics, and Machine Learning-Based Insights into TLR-Targeted Therapeutics.

This review examines how Toll-like receptors recognize Mycoplasma components such as lipoproteins, glycolipids, and CpG-rich DNA, triggering NF-κB and MAPK signaling that can both clear infection and drive chronic inflammatory pathology. The authors integrate cheminformatics and machine learning approaches to identify and prioritize potential TLR-targeted therapeutic compounds. It frames TLR modulation as a strategy for treating Mycoplasma-associated immunopathology.

A Machine Learning-Enhanced Ligand-Based Workflow Identifies Novel Cryptosporidium parvum Inhibitors.

The authors developed a ligand-based virtual screening workflow combining Thompson Sampling, a pharmacophore model, and a machine learning classifier to search 51 million virtual compounds from Enamine's REAL database for new Cryptosporidium parvum inhibitors. This approach identified novel candidate compounds against a parasite for which only one largely ineffective FDA-approved drug exists, addressing a critical unmet need in treating cryptosporidiosis in immunocompromised patients.

Drug Design and Discovery: The Long Road From Hansch Analysis to Artificial Intelligence.

This review traces the historical evolution of QSAR (quantitative structure-activity relationships) from its origins in Hansch analysis through the explosion of molecular descriptors and statistical methods to its current integration with machine learning and artificial intelligence in drug discovery. It highlights how changes in molecular representation and the accumulation of large datasets have driven methodological transformations in the field.

From Generative Molecular Design to Agentic Artificial Intelligence in Drug Discovery.

This review traces the evolution of AI in early-stage drug discovery, from deep generative models adapted from NLP and computer vision for designing small molecules and biologics, to emerging agentic AI systems that can autonomously plan and execute multi-step tasks. It highlights that while state-of-the-art generative models exist, their behavior remains poorly understood, and rapid advances in agentic computational systems are reshaping human-machine interaction in target evaluation and compound design.

QRxVision: Multimodal QR Encoding and Computer Vision for Domain-Specific Drug Discovery.

QRxVision introduces a multimodal framework that combines QR-code-based encoding of molecular data with computer vision to support domain-specific drug discovery. The approach aims to improve high-throughput virtual screening by integrating chemical structure and ligand information into a unified representation. It represents a methodological contribution to computer-aided drug screening rather than a validated new therapeutic finding.

DockBind: A Quality-Controlled Data Set of Modeled Protein-Ligand Complexes Associated with Affinity Data.

DockBind is a curated dataset of modeled protein-ligand complexes paired with experimental binding affinity data, created through a quality-controlled docking workflow. The authors benchmarked free and template-based docking methods along with ligand similarity and maximum common substructure approaches to build the dataset. This resource aims to address the shortage of high-quality training data for machine-learning scoring functions in structure-based drug discovery.

Discovery of potential ALK inhibitors from Glycosmis phytochemicals via integrated machine learning and umbrella sampling approaches.

This study used an integrated computational pipeline—machine learning (CatBoost), molecular docking, molecular dynamics, umbrella sampling, and toxicity prediction—to screen 307 phytochemicals from the Glycosmis genus for potential ALK inhibitors, identifying 26 compounds with predicted binding free energies below -11 kcal/mol. The work highlights promising natural-product candidates for cancer therapy targeting ALK, though experimental validation remains to be done.

Blood-Brain Barrier Permeability Prediction by Integrating Deep Learning Representations with Chemical Compound Knowledge.

This paper presents a multimodal machine learning framework for predicting blood-brain barrier permeability by combining transformer-derived molecular embeddings with traditional physicochemical descriptors through late-stage ensemble fusion. Trained on B3DB and NeuTox datasets and evaluated on the BBBP benchmark, the approach aims to overcome limitations of both descriptor-based methods (lacking structural context) and deep learning methods (prone to overfitting). The model showed strong dataset-dependent predictive performance.

Graphics processing unit-accelerated quantum simulation for molecular biology and drug discovery: algorithms, platforms, and emerging applications.

It covers algorithms, platforms, and emerging applications in molecular biology and drug discovery, arguing that GPU-accelerated quantum simulation enables quantum-accurate modeling of electronic structure and molecular interactions beyond what force fields or DFT alone can achieve.

Machine Learning-Guided Discovery of Novel Inhibitors of Escherichia coli MurB.

The authors built five machine learning models to predict MurB inhibition and used the best one (RDKit_2D-based) to virtually screen an in-house compound library, yielding 238 hits that were then narrowed to 16 candidates via FRED molecular docking. This demonstrates a combined ML-plus-docking workflow for discovering novel antibacterial leads targeting E. coli cell wall biosynthesis.

Crystallographic fragment screening in cancer and antiviral drug discovery: from electron density to translational outcomes.

This review discusses crystallographic fragment screening (CFS) as a structure-guided approach for early-stage drug discovery, particularly in cancer and antiviral research. CFS experimentally identifies where and how small fragment molecules bind to target proteins, providing a validated structural starting point before significant medicinal chemistry investment. The authors argue this reduces early uncertainty and the risk of pursuing binding modes that lack experimental structural support.

Interpretable Drug-Target Prediction via Geometric Alignment: A Linear Alternative to Deep Architectural Complexity.

The authors introduce Multi-View Linear Manifold (MVLM), a linear method that aligns latent embeddings from ChemBERTa (for small molecules) and ESM-2 (for proteins) to predict kinase inhibitor–target interactions. By replacing complex deep architectures with geometric manifold alignment, the approach aims to generalize better to new chemical scaffolds despite limited interaction data. The work is framed as an interpretable alternative to deep-learning drug-target prediction.

AI-Enabled Animal Behavior Analysis for Translational Pharmacology and Therapeutic Discovery.

This review describes how AI methods—including object detection, markerless pose estimation, unsupervised behavioral segmentation, and foundation models—are improving the quantification of animal behavior for preclinical pharmacology and therapeutic discovery. These approaches offer higher spatial, temporal, and phenotypic resolution than conventional manual scoring, which is labor-intensive and hard to reproduce across labs. The authors frame AI-enabled behavioral phenotyping as a more scalable and reproducible endpoint for translational research.
